**Key Factors to Monitor:**


- **P&C Pricing Environment:** Soft market conditions in large account/E&S property and spreading to some casualty lines; management expects continued competitive pressure.
- **Expense & Technology Leverage:** Ongoing digital/AI transformation expected to drive expense ratio improvement and margin support.
- **Capital Deployment:** New **$7.5B** buyback authorization; watch for pace of repurchases and capital return.
- **International Diversification:** Strong growth in Asia and Latin America consumer/retail lines expected to offset US commercial softness.
- **Investment Income:** Continued benefit from higher reinvestment rates and growing private investments.


---


## Summary and Conclusions


- **Chubb enters Q3 2026 earnings off a strong multi-quarter run, but faces tougher YoY comps and a more challenging P&C pricing environment.**
- **Consensus expects modest revenue growth (+3.4% QoQ, +3.8% YoY) and flat-to-down net income/EPS versus prior year, reflecting margin pressure from softening rates and higher loss costs.**
- **Management remains confident in delivering strong operating earnings and double-digit tangible book value growth, citing diversification, disciplined underwriting, and technology-driven efficiency gains.**
- **Key risks include further deterioration in P&C pricing (especially US large account/E&S property and now some casualty), and the ability to maintain underwriting margins as loss costs rise.**
- **Offsetting factors are robust international/consumer growth, higher investment income, and active capital management (buybacks).**

## Guidance and Management Outlook


### Latest Soft Guidance Commentary (Descending Order)


#### Q2 2026 (July 22, 2026)


- Management is "confident in our ability to continue to outperform and to generate strong growth in operating earnings and EPS, and most important, double-digit in tangible book value."
- "We have many sources and handles to pull. I am quite confident. In fact, I am confident in our ability to produce very strong and potentially double-digit EPS growth, and we'll produce strong earnings growth as we go forward."
- "Our fixed income portfolio will continue to generate consistent and growing quarter-to-quarter income. And as we thoughtfully grow our private investments, income from that book, while more variable, will continue to trend higher over time."
- "We're focused on growing \[Chubb Benefits\] organically. We just see a tremendous opportunity to continue growing that business at double digits, and that's our focus. And you know what, over time, as I look at it over the next number of years, it will emerge as a more significant contributor to Chubb's results, top and bottom line."
- "Our combined ratios are sustainable. Obviously, within a reasonable range of variability, but they're sustainable. That's the beauty of the size and scale of the company."
- "We are patient. CATs and FX aside, I'm confident in our ability to continue to outperform and to generate strong growth in operating earnings and EPS, and most important, double-digit in tangible book value, our most important indicator of shareholder wealth."


#### Q1 2026 (Apr 22, 2026)


- "From what I can see, CATs, et cetera, aside, I remain confident in our ability to continue generating strong growth in operating earnings and double-digit growth in EPS and most important, tangible book value."
- "Yes, it is a real growth area for our company over the next 5 years. And by the way, not simply North America, we expect significant growth in various markets internationally that may ultimately dwarf North America."
- "I haven't changed my view of our goals in the last 3 months, and it is steady, and we are executing and we are on track."
- "The technology is evolving at a rapid pace... I think those trends as they emerge will only accelerate, improve, lower cost, make it easier."
- "In the longer term, \[cost of intermediation\] will -- it should decline."


#### Q4 2025 (Feb 4, 2026)


- "While early, we're off to a good start in '26, and we're confident in our ability to generate for the year strong growth in operating earnings and double-digit growth in EPS and tangible book value through the 3 sources of income, P&C underwriting, investment income and life, though cats and FX aside."
- "We expect adjusted net investment income in the first quarter of 2026 to be between **$1.81 billion** to **$1.84 billion** ."
- "We expect our annual core operating effective tax rate for 2026 to be in the range of **19.5%** to **20%** ."


#### Q3 2025 (Oct 22, 2025)


- "We expect to continue generating superior margin and earnings growth and, in fact, an increase to our return on shareholder equity."
- "We estimate that **70%** to **80%** of our businesses present attractive growth opportunities. And looking forward from all we can see, our performance is enduring. We will maintain superior earnings growth, including double-digit growth in EPS, book and tangible book value and core operating ROE increasing to 14-plus percent over the medium term."
- "Increased buyback activity will continue, while at the same time, we will continue to build additional capital and our invested assets."
- "We now expect adjusted net investment income in the fourth quarter to be between **$1.775 billion** and **$1.81 billion** next quarter."
- "We expect our core operating effective tax rate for this full year to be in the range of **19.5%** to **20%** ."

## How Did They Report Last Year? (Q3 2025)


- **Revenue:** **$12,973M** (+ **3.5%** YoY)
- **Net Income:** **$2,477M** (+ **2.8%** YoY)
- **EPS (GAAP):** $6.29 (+ **3.2%** YoY)
- **Core Operating Income:** **$3B** , up **29%**
- **EPS (Core Operating):** $7.49, up **31%**
- **Combined Ratio:** **81.8%** (record low, ~6 pts better YoY)
- **Premium Growth:** Total company + **7.5%** ; Consumer + **16%** , Commercial + **3.3%**
- **Investment Income:** **$1.8B** , up **8.3%**
- **Tangible Book Value Growth:** + **17%** YoY


**Context:** Q3 2025 was a record quarter, with broad-based growth across geographies and segments, strong investment income, and margin expansion. The company benefited from a "quiet cat quarter" and strong prior period development.


---


## Are They Coming Off a Tough Comparable?


**Yes.** Q3 2025 was a record quarter for Chubb, with:


- Core operating income up **29%**
- EPS up **31%**
- Combined ratio at a record low
- Broad-based premium growth, especially in consumer lines


**Q3 2026 faces a tougher YoY comp, especially as P&C pricing softens and loss costs rise.** Consensus expects only modest revenue and EPS growth, with net income and EPS roughly flat to down YoY.


---


## Management Commentary — Key Themes


- **Diversification as a Buffer:** Management repeatedly emphasizes the company's global and product diversification as a key buffer against softening market conditions in US commercial P&C.
- **Expense Discipline and Technology:** Ongoing digital and AI transformation is expected to drive expense savings and support margins, even as top-line growth slows.
- **Capital Returns:** Aggressive buyback activity is expected to continue, supported by strong cash flow and capital generation.
- **Investment Income Tailwind:** Higher reinvestment rates and growing private investments are expected to drive further NII growth.
- **Cautious on Market Conditions:** Management is clear-eyed about softening in property and some casualty lines, but confident in their ability to outperform peers due to discipline and diversification.

## Conclusion


- **Chubb is coming off a record Q3 2025, setting a high bar for Q3 2026.**
- **Consensus expects modest growth, with margin pressure from softening P&C pricing and rising loss costs.**
- **Management remains confident in delivering strong operating earnings, double-digit tangible book value growth, and leveraging diversification and technology to offset market headwinds.**
- **Key factors to watch are the sustainability of underwriting margins, pace of premium growth (especially outside US large account/E&S property), investment income trajectory, and capital return activity.**
